Every Qwen3-8B number in this iteration comes from the 8-bit engine of the screen.




2. *A random displacement of the task-specification states changes the algorithm, and changing the plan noise draw under a fixed seed changes it often.* One direction at alpha 1 changed the algorithm in 17.25 of 20 seeds on the shortest path task, 4.55 on kth smallest and 2.5 on the grid task (pooled contrast against temperature 0.545 [0.41, 0.67], p = 1.0e-5).
3. *The site is the task-specification states at early to middle blocks.* The same displacement at the read position or the condition sentence changed no algorithm at any dose (0 of 526 and 0 of 527 correct programs off the default), the late blocks were almost inert (6 of 521), and at matched downstream displacement the plan site keeps a large advantage (indicator +2.15 [1.79, 2.51]; odds ratio 5.72 [3.94, 8.30]). Blocks 12 to 23 are not distinguished from blocks 0 to 11. *(Correction, iteration 5: two wordings here say more than the experiment supports, that the read position and the condition sentence change nothing at any dose, and that the task-specification states are the site of the choice. Restated: among prefill positions, perturbing the task-specification states changes the algorithm; the read position and the condition sentence are inert at per-position doses up to 4 ban units and far weaker at matched energy (energy-matched read position: +0.23 on find duplicate, Floyd cycle detection 6 of 26 correct programs, and +0.18 on connected components, 5 of 28 off the default); noise in generated tokens 1 to 32 also redirects the choice, more than the plan site on find duplicate (12:0 paired flips at alpha 2 over the 30 pairs, exact McNemar p 0.0005; 6:0 among pairs where both programs are correct). Blocks 0 to 11 against 12 to 23: -0.31 [-0.75, 0.13]. This is a prefill site at which noise is effective, not a locus of the decision, and it is reconciled with the PARTIAL site rule under Inconclusive below.)*
4. *Plan noise is the cheapest knob on some tasks and not on others.* It wins kth smallest (5-point Hill-1 2.72) and connected components (2.09) at no pass cost and loses find duplicate to the iterated veto and the shortest path task to the semantic seed; the preregistered price claim is PARTIAL.

## 5.1 Why this iteration ran what it ran

**Executed results the record had omitted.** Plan noise on the plain prompt, without the prohibition frame of the twin, ran on the same slots and directions as plan noise under the twin frame (Table 173). The frame is not needed on kth smallest, connected components and the shortest path task, and on connected components the plain prompt moved more programs (0.24 against 0.12). The dose units of the experiments differ (Table 174): the ban-free unit is 0.30 to 0.97 of the ban unit across tasks, and substring search, the task that never moves, has by far the largest ban unit. A check made after the rivals were frozen found that the pooled escape fraction does not track the ratio of ban unit to residual norm (Spearman -0.06, AUC 0.49), so movability is not an artefact of the dose unit on the screen tasks.




















**Table 174.** Dose units per task: the ban unit (mean norm of the ban displacement), the ratio of the ban-free unit to it, and both relative to the residual norm. **Table 203.** Panel B landing events. Source: panel B `results/a2_panel.json`.








**Disguised variants.** Of the eight parent and variant pairs, only kth smallest and connected components moved in either form (Table 204), and connected components changed its default under disguise (union find to BFS); the sign of the change in beta and the change in escape fraction agreed in 0 of 1 pair without a default shift, and their Spearman over pairs was 0.13 (p 0.50). Descriptive views that add the remeasured parents (Spearman 0.43, p 0.055, n = 15) or the variants with a permutation that preserves clusters (0.54, p 0.015, n = 22) are positive, as is the screen view (0.79 on the 15 screen tasks), but none is the preregistered test.

**The base repertoire against movability: screen, confirmation and second family.** The same quantity, beta against the escape fraction, was measured five ways in this iteration, and the answer depends on which tasks enter. The figure plots both sets. The landing half replicates everywhere it could be measured: the base runner-up named the push landing on 5 of 5 movable existing tasks (screen), 3 of 3 in panel A, 3 of 4 in panel B and 5 of 7 in Gemma, 16 of 19 events in all.

**Movability depends on the engine and the unit.** Table 222 sets the existing tasks' movability side by side across the measurements of iterations 4 and 5. Under iteration 4's 8-bit engine and the ban unit, six tasks were movable; under this iteration's bf16 engine and the ban-free unit, only kth smallest and connected components escape with 8 fixed directions, and per-sample plan noise moves more than 10% of programs off the default only on kth smallest (0.28 at alpha 2). On the shortest path task, per-sample plan noise moved 26% of programs at alpha 1 in iteration 4 and 0% at alpha 1 here (4% at alpha 2, about 1.7 ban units). Those two directions therefore do not explain the difference, and its cause is not established here. Movability is therefore a property of a task under a given engine, unit and direction population, and the confirmation panels measured it under bf16 and the ban-free unit only.

## 5.12 What the next iteration takes from this one

The narrowed repertoire account split in two. Its landing half held in both families and on unseen tasks: when a nudge moves the instruct model, it moves it to the algorithm the base model writes next, and a forecast built from base samples, before any push, names that landing better than the model's stated alternative. Its movability half failed on unseen tasks: a base model that writes many algorithms does not mark a task the instruct model can be nudged off, and its states, written into the instruct prefill, reopen the choice on one task in five. The base repertoire marks where a nudge can lead, not whether it can lead anywhere.

The open question is therefore what makes a task diverse in the base immovable. Count primes and valid anagram (beta 0.81 each) never moved, while trapped rain water (0.23) did. Two leads came out of this iteration's data. In panel A the three units that moved had an alternative at least twice as fast as the default and the three that did not had none, although median of two sorted lists broke the pattern. And in the transplant experiment early blocks 0 to 11 moved kth smallest and connected components more than the main band, which suggests the narrowing sits at least partly upstream of blocks 12 to 23. The positioning audit names the baselines a further test needs: weight interpolation between the base and instruct models, layer restoration at the transplant's block ranges, and token-level base and aligned collaboration [92, 93, 94, 102]. Base intent, which beat plan noise on three of five tasks, is the strongest practical knob the run has priced, and it is itself a form of that collaboration at the level of sentences. Finally, movability has to be measured under the engine and unit at which it will be used: the six screen-movable tasks of iteration 4 shrank to two under bf16 and the ban-free unit, for reasons this iteration did not establish.

# What we have learned so far

After five iterations the run has a firm picture of the collapse, a complete answer on temperature, a prefill site at which noise is effective (not a locus of the decision, and no representation of the choice), a measured but incomplete account of what a prohibition does, and a split verdict on where the alternatives come from. Qwen3-8B [5] writes BFS and Dijkstra almost without exception on the two path search tasks and one algorithm on each of 13 further coding tasks (modal share 1.00 on 12, 0.98 on one). Sampling temperature, top-k, top-p, min-p, thinking mode and random context seeds change how the code is worded, not which algorithm it implements. With the token seed coupled across temperatures from 0.3 to 1.3, the algorithm changed in 0 of 20 seeds on three tasks with thinking off. It also changed in 0 of 20 on the shortest path task with thinking on, under top-p 1 and under top-k 10. Meanwhile the number of phrasings per idea rose from 3 to 13 on the grid task. Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct [22] attempts more algorithms but its correct grid programs are BFS 20 of 20, and gemma-3-4b-it [76] shows the same temperature null (best Hill-1 within 5 pass points at most 1.32). On other problems temperature above 1 has been reported to raise algorithmic diversity at a correctness cost [72], so the null belongs to these tasks.

The algorithm can be influenced, and where it can depends on the task, and on the engine and dose unit at which it is measured. Under the 8-bit engine of iteration 4, a random displacement of the task-specification states at early to middle layers, sized to the displacement a ban itself causes, changes the algorithm the model writes. Single random directions at that size changed it in 3 to 17 of 20 coupled seeds on the shortest path task, against 0 for temperature (17.25 of 20 for the union over subsets of three directions). The same displacement at the read position or on the condition sentence changes nothing at per-position doses up to 4 ban units (0 of 526 and 0 of 527 correct programs off the default). At matched energy it is far weaker but not inert (+0.23 on find duplicate, +0.18 on connected components). The late layers are almost inert, and the advantage of the task-specification site survives matching on downstream displacement (odds ratio 5.72 [3.94, 8.30]). Noise in generated tokens 1 to 32 also redirects the choice, more than the plan site on find duplicate, so the choice is still open after prefill. Under the bf16 engine and the ban-free dose unit of iteration 5, however, only kth smallest and connected components escape with fixed random directions, and per-sample plan noise moves more than 10% of programs off the default only on kth smallest; the cause of this shrinkage is not established.



Where pushes move the model, the base model says where they will land. Given the same prompt under the chat template, the untuned base model spreads over more algorithms than the instruct model on most tasks (5 of the 15 existing tasks are diverse in the base and 7 intermediate). Its most frequent alternative is where the instruct model goes when nudged. This held on 5 of 5 movable existing tasks, on 6 of 7 events on new tasks (Poisson-binomial p 0.003) and on 5 of 7 in Gemma (p 0.025), and in panel A no nudged program landed outside the base repertoire. A forecast built from base samples, before any push, beats the model's own stated alternative on log score (by 0.75 nats on new tasks and 1.50 in Gemma). The base model does not, however, say whether a task can be nudged at all: on unseen tasks the base off-default share ranks movability at Spearman 0.15 (13 units), tasks diverse in the base such as count primes and valid anagram (0.81 each) never moved, and simpler rivals (the runtime merit of the fastest alternative, the twin's own modal share) tracked movability better. Writing the base model's task-specification states into the instruct prefill reopened the base runner-up on 1 of 5 Qwen3-8B tasks diverse in the base and 2 of 7 Gemma tasks. In Gemma both successes were tasks whose instruct twin already wrote the runner-up 8% to 12% of the time. On kth smallest a random displacement of the same norm moved more programs than the base states. Post-training narrowed what the base model writes, consistent with reports that it narrows output diversity [57, 35, 87], and the narrowed alternatives are where nudges land; but the narrowing is not carried by the task-specification states of blocks 12 to 23 alone.

Where the choice is represented is not established. The task-specification states are a site at which noise is effective; a subspace spanned by the centroids of forced-algorithm prompts there is reliable (split-half cosine 0.89 to 0.97) yet does not predict which random directions move the algorithm (within-task Spearman 0.03), and removing the component of a push in it leaves the effect intact. Which directions move the algorithm is reproducible across templates on four tasks (0.76 to 0.90) and less so on the grid task (0.39) and find duplicate (0.59), and signed progress toward the runner-up, the one exploratory predictor, concentrated on connected components and was closed.









No instruction, knob, push or transplant produced a correct novel algorithm. Iterations 1 to 3 produced 116 correct programs outside the catalogue, and none was new. In iteration 4 none of 14,206 correct programs of the site and subspace experiments was new. In iteration 5, 130 correct programs outside the catalogue, from the base model, the transplant, the panels, the knobs and Gemma, were all labeller misses, known techniques outside the frozen catalogue, catalogue variants or degenerate. The long-form instruction of the request makes most outputs claim novelty while their code is a catalogue algorithm or absent. Within single-sample generation the reachable ideas are the model's known catalogue and, where nudges act, its base model's repertoire; search with an evaluator, which this run did not test, is the documented route to new programs [81, 82].
